title: Truth Matters
subtitle: Gospel truths, misleading messages, and science that changed its mind

metadata.sourceMaterial: Youth lesson from a Latter-day Saint perspective. Questions reviewed with the teacher. Accept equivalent wording; the premortal life and the pre-existence are both accepted answers.

categories.title: Science: They Believed WHAT?!
categories.sourceMaterial: These are old explanations people believed. Better evidence helped people discover their mistakes. Sources by value: 200 — https://www.royalsociety.org/blog/2023/08/diet-of-worms/ ; 400 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12795547/ ; 600 — https://www.mun.ca/biology/scarr/4270_Redi_experiment.html ; 800 — https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/eid/article/12/7/ET-1207_article ; 1000 — https://www.nlm.nih.gov/exhibition/artificial-intelligence-and-physiognomy/digitalgallery_theme_1.html

clues.clue: People once believed tiny creatures were chewing holes inside their teeth. What creatures did they blame?
clues.response: Worms. ‘Tooth worms’ were an old explanation for toothache and decay.

clues.clue: Some ancient thinkers believed we could see because rays shot OUT of which body parts?
clues.response: Our eyes. This was called the emission theory of vision.

clues.clue: People once thought rotting meat produced maggots by itself. Maggots actually hatch from eggs laid by which insects?
clues.response: Flies. Experiments showed that keeping flies away prevented maggots from appearing on the meat.

clues.clue: Malaria was once blamed on ‘bad air’ from swamps. Which insects actually spread the parasites that cause it?
clues.response: Mosquitoes. The name ‘malaria’ comes from the Italian for ‘bad air.’

clues.clue: Phrenologists claimed they could tell your personality by feeling bumps on which part of your body?
clues.response: Your skull. Also accept: your head. This supposed way of reading someone’s character was discredited.
